note: Stage 1 text must show potential problems only - never solutions, methods, products or costs. Placeholders: {elevation} {distance} {travel}. Set approved to true only when Stuart has signed the rule off.

rules.trigger: Per elevation: distance to the drawn site boundary that wall faces (ADB 13.5 / Diagram 13.2: faces test plus the 80 degree rule, measured at right angles from the wall) under 25 m. Distances from background-checks.js pcBgFacingBoundaryDistances. The cladding fire rating is not asked; standard PIR is never treated as unprotected by default. No facing boundary marked = need info, never ok.
rules.stage1Problem: A fire-rated wall may be needed on elevation {elevation}. Your building supplier should confirm.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: A wall close to a boundary has to limit how far fire can spread to your neighbour's land.
rules.needInfo: Boundary on elevation {elevation} not marked (mark every site boundary in Site Layout)

rules.trigger: Per elevation: distance to the boundary that wall faces (same facing distances as B_BOUNDARY) under 1 m. A line passing a corner is measured at right angles from the wall, not diagonally to the corner. No facing boundary marked = need info.
rules.stage1Problem: Elevation {elevation} is under 1 m from the boundary, so the strictest fire rules apply to this wall.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: Walls this close face the tightest limits. This can affect the wall and any doors or windows in it.
rules.needInfo: Boundary on elevation {elevation} not marked (mark every site boundary in Site Layout)

rules.trigger: Mean roof height ((eaves + ridge) / 2) over 10 m.
rules.stage1Problem: Your building may need a fire safety check because of its height.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: Taller buildings are judged differently for fire spread.

rules.trigger: Mean roof height ((eaves + ridge) / 2) over 18 m - same height definition as B_HEIGHT_10M, not ridge height.
rules.stage1Problem: Your building is over 18 m high (measured to mid-roof), so stricter wall rules may apply.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: Taller buildings face tighter fire safety rules.

rules.regsRef: ADB Vol 2 Section 15 Table 15.1 note 2 / Table 15.2
rules.trigger: Always a customer-scope note: fire engine access is for the customer's professional team. No inputs needed.
rules.stage1Note: Fire engine access – ask a professional to check

rules.trigger: B_BOUNDARY flagged AND eaves height over 7 m.
rules.stage1Problem: The frame and base near the boundary may need extra checks.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: A tall wall close to a boundary can change how the frame and base are designed.
rules.needInfo: Boundary distances and the building height

rules.trigger: Furthest point in plan to nearest personnel or fire-exit door, straight line x 1.5. Limits: normal hazard 45 m (exits in 2+ directions) / 25 m (one direction); flammable storage 25 m / 12 m. Roller doors and doors into another building do not count.
rules.stage1Problem: The furthest point is about {travel} m from an exit. This may be too far.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: People inside must be able to reach an exit within a set distance if there is a fire.
rules.needInfo: Personnel exits in Building Design, and what will be stored

rules.trigger: People = floor area / 30 m2 (storage) or / 5 m2 (production). Over 60 people AND fewer than 2 exits.
rules.stage1Problem: Your building may need more fire exits.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: A building this size can hold more people than one exit is allowed to serve.
rules.needInfo: The building use, width and length

rules.regsRef: Approved Document L Vol 2 (2021: para 0.11, 2.27–2.29; 2026 edition: para 0.12, 2.26–2.28)
rules.trigger: Test is fixed heating or cooling. Heated, other temperature requirement, or services answer Yes = note. Unheated (Stage 1 heated answer) AND services No AND use inside the exemption (industrial, workshop, agricultural) = ok. Unheated AND services No AND any other use (e.g. storage, distribution, sports or leisure) = check line (never ok). Heated answer, services answer or use unknown = need info (never ok).
rules.stage1Problem: Building Control may ask for an energy assessment for this unheated {use} building. Ask a professional to check.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: The energy exemption for unheated buildings does not clearly cover storage.
rules.stage1Note: If the building has heating, cooling, toilets, offices or other services, Building Control may ask for an energy assessment. Ask a professional to check.
rules.needInfo: Whether the building will have heating, toilets, offices or other services
rules.needInfoHeating: Whether the building will be heated or cooled

rules.trigger: England only. Reads Building Design / Site Layout data: footprint (width x length), ridge height, boundary distance on each elevation, free-standing or extension, existing building floor area and height. New free-standing building over 200 m2 = not PD. Extension over the lesser of 50% of the existing floor area or 1,000 m2 = not PD. Any part within 5 m of the boundary = not PD. Within 10 m of the boundary: max height 5 m. Otherwise a new building is no higher than the tallest building on site and max 15 m; an extension is no higher than the building it extends. Any missing answer, or an unmarked boundary side = need info. Scotland or Wales = need info (different rules).
rules.stage1Problem: Full planning permission is likely to be needed. Ask a planning professional to check.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: The size, height or distance to the boundary looks too big for the simpler planning route.

rules.regsRef: Building Regulations 2010 Sch 2 Class 4 (temporary) and Class 6 (small detached)
rules.trigger: Detached, no sleeping accommodation, floor area up to 30 m2; OR temporary building up 28 days or less.
rules.stage1Note: This building may be exempt from Building Regulations. Ask a professional to confirm.
rules.needInfo: Whether the building is detached, has sleeping accommodation, or is temporary

rules.regsRef: Part A / BS EN 1991 site loads
rules.trigger: Quote request carries postcode, altitude, site exposure and planned roof solar panels (added roof load). Any missing = need info.
rules.needInfo: Site altitude, site exposure and whether roof solar is planned

rules.trigger: Per elevation: distance to boundary under closeM. Boundary = drawn boundary lines or the per-elevation answers; other buildings on the same site are not boundaries. Quote request only.
rules.needInfo: Boundary on elevation {elevation} not marked (mark every site boundary in Site Layout)

rules.trigger: Quote request: roller and sectional doors are not fire exits; building over 25 m deep (longer plan dimension) = at least one personnel door per long side.

rules.regsRef: ADB Vol 2 Section 14 rooflights (exact table UNKNOWN - to verify)
rules.trigger: Rooflights = Yes AND (an elevation under boundaryM from the boundary OR a fire wall present).
rules.stage1Problem: There are limits on rooflights near a boundary or fire wall.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: Rooflights close to a boundary or fire wall face limits on size and position.
rules.needInfo: Whether there are rooflights, and the boundary or fire wall details

rules.regsRef: AD L Vol 2 (limiting U-value for rooflights 2.2 - as supplied, not re-verified)
rules.trigger: Heated building AND rooflights = Yes. Quote request only.
rules.needInfo: Whether there are rooflights, and whether the building is heated

rules.trigger: Heating/toilets/offices/services = Yes (fact regsServices).
rules.stage1Problem: Rules on access for disabled people apply to this building.
rules.stage1WhyItMatters: Buildings with staff facilities must be reachable and usable by disabled people.
rules.stage2Solution: A level threshold and an accessible door are needed.
rules.needInfo: Whether the building will have heating, toilets, offices or other services

rules.trigger: Unheated building AND vehicles or wet goods = Yes. Advice only, never a fail.
rules.stage2Solution: Consider anti-condensation roof sheets or vents.
rules.needInfo: Whether the building is heated, and whether vehicles or wet goods are used

rules.trigger: Always (England). Quote request: gutters and downpipes by the building supplier; surface water connection is customer scope. Also covers services or drainage within the footprint (was the separate services/drainage check). Built inside an existing building (Stage 1 base answer 'Existing building / structure', or a use saying inside/within an existing building) = services line only, no gutter or surface water lines.
rules.stage1Note: Rainwater drainage, and any drains or services under the building, can change where it can go, how the base is built and how long the job takes. Ask a professional to check.
rules.stage1NoteInternal: Any services or drainage within the footprint (these may affect the building position, foundations or programme) – get professional support.

rules.regsRef: AD L 2026 edition, applies from 24 Mar 2027 (England)
rules.trigger: Heated buildings only (project details). A customer-scope note; no dates are asked.
rules.stage2Solution: Personnel doors at U 1.6. Energy calculation favours low-carbon heating.
rules.stage1Note: The building will be heated, so newer energy rules (2027) may apply. Ask a professional to check.

rules.regsRef: Stage 1 question: what is on the area where the building will sit (customer scope)
rules.trigger: Existing surface answer is Tarmac / asphalt, Hardcore / stone, Soil / grass, Existing building / structure or Mixed = surface does not confirm a slab. Answer Not sure = base information incomplete. Concrete slab = nothing shown. Old saved answer 'Existing building' counts as 'Existing building / structure'.
rules.stage1Problem: What is on the ground now does not prove it can carry the building. A structural engineer should check.
rules.stage1ProblemNotSure: We don't yet know if the ground can take the building. A structural engineer should check.

rules.regsRef: Stage 1 answer: is the site level
rules.trigger: Level answer No or Not sure = levels warning. Level answer No = also a need-info line. (The level question is not currently asked, so this only fires on older projects that have an answer.)
rules.stage1Problem: Uneven or unknown ground levels can affect the base, drainage, door thresholds and fitting the building.
rules.needInfo: Ground levels: you said the site is not level, so we treat this as unconfirmed.

rules.trigger: Programme answer is exactly '0–3 months' = short-programme warning.
rules.stage1Problem: Your timescale is tight. Approvals, design, groundworks, manufacture and fitting all take time.

rules.regsRef: Site Layout map: building position and site boundary
rules.trigger: Building position not confirmed on the map = one need-info line. Site boundary not confirmed on the map = one need-info line. Anything other than 'confirmed' (skipped, blank, old values) counts as not confirmed.
rules.needInfoPosition: Building position not yet confirmed on a site map.
rules.needInfoBoundary: Site boundary not yet confirmed on a site map.
